trick: One-page spec, then a fresh session
source_note: Harper Reed's workflow (write spec.md, then build from it); Anthropic's best practices also suggest a spec, then a fresh session. With: step 1 is the spec prefix plus the task text, headless; step 2 is a NEW session in the same repo copy (no --resume) with 'Implement SPEC.md. Run its end-to-end check before you finish.' Step 2 sees the task only through SPEC.md, so a constraint the spec drops is lost; that is part of the trick and is logged. Without: the standard single call. Time, cost, turns and tokens summed over both steps; the 20-minute cap covers both.

with.label: SPEC.md first, then a fresh session builds it
with.prompt_prefix: Don't change any code yet. Read the relevant code, then write a one-page SPEC.md for the task below: the goal, the files and interfaces involved, what is out of scope, and an end-to-end check that proves it works. Then stop.

turns.prompt: Implement SPEC.md. Run its end-to-end check before you finish.
